blocks.text: Docker never garbage-collects on its own: images, build cache, stopped containers, volumes and logs accumulate until the disk fills.

$ docker system df          # images, containers, volumes, build cache + reclaimable
$ docker system df -v       # per object

rows: All images unused by any container
Stopped containers and their writable layers

blocks.text:
$ docker image prune -a --filter "until=168h"
$ docker builder prune --keep-storage 10GB

items: Dangling = untagged leftovers from rebuilding a tag; always safe to remove.
"Unused" means not attached to any container right now, not "unimportant".

blocks.text: `docker system prune -a --volumes` deletes the database volumes of stopped Compose projects. On CI, pruning everything destroys the layer cache; prune by age and cap cache size instead. Container logs aren't shown by system df and need rotation.

Q: "A build host keeps running out of disk. What's your policy?" A: "Measure with docker system df, cap BuildKit cache with keep-storage, prune images by age on a schedule, configure log rotation, and never prune volumes blindly."

items: Dangling ≠ unused; prune -a removes all unused images.
Build cache is usually the biggest consumer.
Prune by age and size limits, not "everything".
